auth.title: Authorize with Duke Energy
auth.description:
1. Turn on iPhone emulation before opening the sign-in link. Use an iPhone preset in Chrome's device toolbar or Firefox's Responsive Design Mode. Changing only the User-Agent is not enough in Chrome because it also reports its platform through client hints.
2. [Open Duke Energy sign-in]({authorize_url}) and sign in. Stay in that tab. Use this link, not the public Duke Energy website.
3. Copy the entire address after Duke redirects. It starts with `{callback_prefix}` and contains a `code` parameter.
4. Paste the address into **Callback URL** below and submit.

Keep this setup form open until you submit the URL. Treat the callback URL as a sign-in credential; keep it out of issue reports and screenshots. Turn off device emulation when you are done.

Home Assistant then imports up to three years of usage. This can take a minute or two; leave the integration in place while it initializes.

iPhone User-Agent, if your emulation mode or extension asks for one:
`{user_agent}`

init.title: Cost tracking
init.description: Configure how energy cost is recorded alongside usage. Pick a meter to set its cost source, then choose Save to apply.

data_description.meter: Choose a meter to configure, or Save and apply to finish.

meter.title: Cost source
meter.description:
### Set the cost source for {meter}.

- **Entity price:** the rate in {unit}. A `sensor` uses long-term statistics to price usage over its history; a `number`/`input_number` act as static price.
- **Static price:** a fixed rate in {unit}.

data_description.entity_id: Pick a sensor, number, or input_number holding the rate in {unit}.
data_description.price: Used when the cost source is Static. Enter the rate in {unit}.

data_description.backfill_cost: Reprice all stored consumption for every meter with cost tracking enabled. This uses the earliest available or static price and replaces historical cost values. Leave off to keep existing costs and catch up unpriced usage at the next poll.
